title: Redesigning quantum theory
abstract: QBism understands quantum mechanics to be probability theory supplemented by additional nonclassical coherence conditions. In this dissertation, we develop these nonclassical coherence conditions from first principles, emphasizing the role of a well chosen reference measurement. After treating standard probability on subjective Bayesian lines, we demonstrate an equivalence between the QBist approach and the existing framework of generalized probabilistic theories. We show that the fundamental nonclassical coherence relation may almost always be taken to be a gentle modification of the law of total probability, and give a coherentist account of when an experimental scenario has a classical explanation. Finally, we show that when the reference measurement is chosen to correspond to a complex projective 3-design, the shape of quantum state space is implicit in the probabilities which characterize the reference measurement itself. Thus coherence with this single reference measurement, properly understood, implies coherence with all of finite dimensional quantum mechanics. We then attempt a modest reconstruction of quantum theory along these lines, one practical consequence of which is a method for self-testing complex projective $t$-designs for $t\ge 3$ in a theory-agnostic way.
summary: This dissertation attempts a foundational reconstruction of quantum theory by interpreting it through the lens of QBism, viewing quantum mechanics as probability theory augmented by specific nonclassical coherence rules. The authors derive these rules from first principles, showing that coherence with a specific type of reference measurement is sufficient to imply the entire structure of finite-dimensional quantum mechanics. It offers a novel, theory-agnostic method for self-testing these underlying mathematical structures.
main_problem: The paper aims to redesign quantum theory by deriving its fundamental nonclassical coherence conditions from first principles, moving beyond standard interpretations.
main_result: Coherence with a single reference measurement corresponding to a complex projective 3-design is shown to imply coherence with all of finite dimensional quantum mechanics.
method: The authors use a QBist framework, treating quantum mechanics as probability theory supplemented by nonclassical coherence conditions, and comparing this to generalized probabilistic theories.
model_or_system: The focus is on the abstract mathematical structure of quantum theory itself, particularly the relationship between subjective probability assignments, reference measurements, and the Born rule.
key_observables: Probabilities assigned to measurement outcomes, quantum states (represented by density matrices), and the structure of the state space.
important_parameters: The choice of the reference measurement (especially those related to complex projective $t$-designs, $t\ge 3$).
main_assumptions: The fundamental nonclassical coherence relation can be derived from first principles, often by approximating it as a gentle modification of the law of total probability.
paper_structure: The dissertation is structured logically, starting with an introduction covering foundations and QBism, moving through probability theory derivations, analyzing the Born identity, and concluding with discussions on the Bloch form and reconstruction of quantum theory.
why_interesting: This work tackles the foundational axioms of quantum mechanics, which underpins all applications in AMO physics, by re-deriving the core rules from subjective probability principles.
